title: Dallas Fed Trimmed Mean PCE (Sep 2026 data) — the energy-shock month read on a gauge that trims energy out
source: EST: dallasfed.org/research/pce fetched direct 2026-09-15 states verbatim that "Updates to the Trimmed Mean PCE Inflation Rate follow BEA's release schedule for Personal Income and Outlays data", and carries July 2026 data (1-month 2.2%, 6-month 2.3%, 12-month 2.3%) with its next update given as September 30. The date here is therefore derived from that stated rule plus BEA's own confirmed 08:30 ET slot for September-data Personal Income and Outlays — bea.gov/news/schedule, re-fetched and structurally parsed 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200, 75,123 bytes), reading verbatim "October 29 8:30 AM · News · Personal Income and Outlays, September 2026". Filed `estimate` on three counts that are not date doubt: the date is derived from a publisher's stated rule rather than named on a dated Dallas Fed calendar entry (the same derivation shape eia-weekly-petroleum-status-2026-09-16 recorded), this file's confirmed-prefix taxonomy defines no prefix for a regional Reserve Bank research release, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: Discovered during the pce-2026-10-29 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-15, D-44). Sibling to the proposed dallas-fed-trimmed-mean-2026-09-30, and filed for a DIFFERENT reason. The 09-30 edition answers whether the BEA annual update moved the center of the distribution or only trimmed its edges. This one answers the question September itself poses: the trimmed mean discards the largest movers in both tails, and September 2026 is the month the energy tail exploded — EIA weekly regular gasoline $4.071 (08-31) -> $4.157 (09-07) -> $4.319 (09-14), Brent $88.29 (08-28) -> $107.46 (09-15). So on one morning the calendar gets headline PCE (energy fully in), core PCE (energy out, but energy-driven services pass-through in) and trimmed mean (extremes out of both) on the same reference month. That three-way spread is the cleanest available test of the pce-2026-10-29 ledger's standing two-sided rule -- core cooling is measurement, headline heat is energy -- and it is the gauge that scores that ledger's leg 8, its own unsourced inference that the trimmed mean absorbs the 09-30 revision LESS than core does because portfolio management at 21.6% annual price growth is exactly what a trimmed mean discards. It also feeds the measure-selection question the same ledger's leg 7 left open: Chair Warsh states a preference for trimmed mean but argued the hawkish case at Jackson Hole on 2026-08-28 from headline PCE 3.7%/4.1%, while July trimmed mean read 2.3% -- a ~100bp wedge, and September is precisely the configuration that widens it. Impact filed `medium`, not `high`: it publishes into the same 08:30 ET minute as the September PCE print and the Q3 advance GDP estimate inside a 43-event corridor, so its own tape contribution is unattributable; the value is informational, not directional. `symbols: []` -- no house playbook is macro-keyed to it and nothing here licenses a position. If the lane that researches this id judges the trimmed mean a sub-reading of the PCE release rather than an event of its own, this proposal is inert and costs nothing.
